Who was Giacomo Casanova, the man whose name became synonymous with romance and seduction? Was he really the world's most famous lover, or was there much more to his extraordinary life?
Born in 18th-century Venice, Casanova was a man of many identities a priest-in-training, soldier, gambler, spy, writer and master storyteller. He moved among European royalty, helped establish France's national lottery, fooled wealthy aristocrats with tales of magic and mystery, and even escaped from Venice's notorious Piombi prison using nothing but an iron nail, a Bible and a plate covered in butter.
